extracted.intended_audience: tourists/travellers planning a visit to Edinburgh
extracted.subtask_description: Selecting and planning visits to Edinburgh attractions: choosing which sites to visit, when to go, what to expect (duration, difficulty, costs, and on-site facilities) and how to prepare for each experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Curated, not ranked list
rubrics_metrics.description: The list was created by VisitScotland to showcase a range of experiences; it isn’t ranked in any specific order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the list as a sampler of varied experiences rather than a 'top-to-bottom' ranking; pick items that match your interests and constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best time of day / beat the crowds
rubrics_metrics.description: Advice to travel mid-morning to beat the crowds (Arthur’s Seat) and to choose a morning slot for Edinburgh Castle as it gets busier throughout the day. Calton Hill is recommended 'during golden hour' for its views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule high-demand attractions early in the day or at recommended times (golden hour for views) to avoid crowds and get the best lighting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-booking and advance ticketing
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid disappointment, book online a few weeks prior to visiting major attractions (example: Edinburgh Castle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check attraction booking requirements and reserve time slots/tickets in advance when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guided tours vs. self-guided visits
rubrics_metrics.description: Guided tours (e.g., castle 30-minute guided tour, Real Mary King’s Close 60-minute tour) are presented as providing deeper learning and engaging narration (even theatrical re-enactment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider paying extra for a guided tour if you want detailed historical context or an enhanced experience; tour length and format vary by attraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical difficulty and route selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Walking routes are colour-coded and vary in difficulty (Arthur’s Seat Green Route = easier, perfect for families); Calton Hill is a short, easy paved walk. Advice to wear sturdy shoes and warm clothing due to chill and terrain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match route choice to fitness and group composition, wear appropriate footwear/clothing, and choose easier routes for children or less-able visitors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration and timed/sessioned experiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Attractions include fixed-duration experiences: Real Mary King’s Close (60-minute tour), Lost Shore Surf Resort (90-minute session with 30-minute safety briefing + 60 minutes in water), and Dynamic Earth (allocated time for the 360° planetarium dome show).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan your itinerary around stated durations and allocated time slots; arrive punctually for timed shows/sessions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weather considerations / indoor vs outdoor planning
rubrics_metrics.description: The National Museum of Scotland is recommended for rainy days (free admission, indoor exhibits); outdoor sites like Arthur’s Seat can be chilly and require warm clothing; Lost Shore’s wavepool is heated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have indoor alternatives for bad weather and check temperature/comfort details for outdoor activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability for families and children
rubrics_metrics.description: Several attractions are explicitly flagged family-friendly (Arthur’s Seat Green Route, National Museum 'aimed for the young and the young at heart', Camera Obscura as fun for kids).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose attractions with hands-on or easy-access features when travelling with children; check age-appropriate exhibits and facilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission cost, free options, and value for money
rubrics_metrics.description: Some attractions have free admission (National Museum of Scotland) while others require paid tickets or optional paid extras (guided tours, tastings). The author comments on perceived value (e.g., Lost Shore pizza 'excellent value for money').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm admission fees, free-entry options, and what is included to assess value before visiting.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-site food and refreshment availability
rubrics_metrics.description: On-site dining options are noted: Cafe Calton at Calton Hill, a canteen and multiple food vendors at Lost Shore Surf Resort, and a distillery bar at Edinburgh Gin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factor meal/refreshment availability into plans; some sites offer casual dining or bars where you can recharge between activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photography and access restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Some attractions have photography rules (e.g., no photos inside the Palace of Holyroodhouse) while others offer scenic rooftop terraces and free binoculars/telescopes for viewing (Camera Obscura).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect photography policies and bring a camera for permitted viewpoint areas; check restrictions before visiting exhibits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive and experiential content
rubrics_metrics.description: Many attractions emphasize hands-on or participatory experiences: interactive museum exhibits, surfing lessons with coaching, making a whisky-based cocktail at Johnnie Walker, touching a real iceberg and animatronics at Dynamic Earth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect and plan for participatory elements (wear suitable clothing for activities, be prepared to take part in tastings or physical experiences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and accessibility supports
rubrics_metrics.description: Some attractions provide language aids and accessibility resources (Holyrood Palace tickets included a free audio guide available in different languages).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for audio guides, language options, and other accessibility supports when booking if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unique/local flavour and novelty experiences
rubrics_metrics.description: The list highlights unique Edinburgh/local experiences (Scotland’s first surfing resort at Ratho, Johnnie Walker and Edinburgh Gin distillery experiences, limited-edition local bottle flavours like 'Salt N Sauce').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek out experiences that showcase local culture or unusual attractions for a distinct visit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical/educational depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Some attractions offer substantial historical content (Edinburgh Castle covering centuries of history and royal residence, Real Mary King’s Close recounting 17th-century living conditions and plague, museum artefacts and the Millenium Clock's 20th-century narrative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate extra time if you want to dive into historical exhibits and narratives; guided tours often enhance educational value.
